newsitem.title: UK: Med products steady to firmer.
newsitem.headline: Med products steady to firmer.

text.p: Oil products were steady to firmer in the Mediterranean market on Monday, traders said.

A refiner in France, who bought healthy quantities of low sulphur material last week, was heard to have bought on Friday a low sulphur straight-run Russian cargo from a refiner in Italy at around $6 over the quoted cif high.
Another refiner bought a bunker piece from a different refiner in France, also on Friday, at around $5 over fob high.
A trader was heard to have sold another Russian cargo to the same refinery buyer but further details of the deal were not known.
A Mersin cargo, heard offered on Friday by a U.K. major, was believed to have been sold, possibly into Spain.
Gas oil differentials were stable but trade was inactive with outright prices easing $1 a tonne in line with August IPE, which closed weaker at $162.50.
Offers for 0.2 percent sulphur Russian heating oil were around cif high quotes +$2.50 basis Genoa, with bids coming in $1 lower.
Low sulphur diesel was tight with refiners remaining reluctant to produce the more expensive material bcause of the meagre spread to heating oil.
Only one July cargo was seen in the hands of a seller.

Attention remained focused on the results due out this week of a Turkish tender for 75,000 tonnes of both 0.5 and 0.2 percent sulphur gas oil and a Syrian tender for 100,000 tonnes of 0.7 percent sulohur gas oil.
Naphtha was quiet, with levels valued a touch lower on weaker swaps and on an NWE cargo deal at $191, well below bid-offer talk of Friday.
The arb to Asia was argued by some to have closed after recent large-scale deals for shipments in July/August, although the arb to the U.S. was still seen possible.
A Benelux trader/refiner was rumored bidding for gasoline in the Med at $197, reflecting the emerging market view that the cargo premium over barges for European mogas was widening.
